sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered [MATH: x,y,z] on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

[MATH: x + y − 3z = 5; − 7x − y + z = 0; 2x + y − 2z = − 2]

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

[MATH: \left\lbrack \matrix { 1 & 1 & -3 \ -7 & -1 & 1 \ 2 & 1 & -2 } \right\rbrack]

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

[MATH: 1|1|− 3|5; − 7|− 1|1|0; 2|1|− 2|− 2]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can use matrices to solve systems of linear equations. To do this, we need to set up the augmented matrix for the system.

Content:
As an example, let's consider the system of equations below.

Content:
[MATH: 2x + 5y = − 1; − 3x + 7y = 1]

Content:
First, we find the coefficient matrix, which consists of the coefficients of the variables:
[MATH: 2|5; − 3|7]

Content:
Then, we create the augmented matrix. This is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

Content:
[MATH: 2|5|− 1; − 3|7|1]

Content:
In the future, we will learn how to use coefficient and augmented matrices to solve systems of equations. But for now, let's practice setting them up.

---

Item 2 — Tutorial: The Order of the Variables in a Linear System

Content:
We will use mostly systems with the following variables:

Content:
- [MATH: x,y,z,] or
- [MATH: x_1,x_2,x_3,] or
- [MATH: a,b,c.]

Content:
These sets of variables will always have a natural order:

Content:
- alphabetical order in the case of [MATH: x,y,z] or [MATH: a,b,c,] and
- numerical order in the case of [MATH: x_1, x_2, x_3.]

---

Item 3 — Example: Finding the Coefficient Matrix of a System of Linear Equations

Example Prompt:
What is the coefficient matrix for the following system of linear equations?

[MATH: {x − 2y = 1; 2y = − 1]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we organize the system so that every variable has a coefficient:

[MATH: x − 2y = 1; 0x + 2y = − 1]

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

[MATH: \left\lbrack
\matrix {
1 & -2 \
0 & 2
}
\right\rbrack]

Example Prompt:

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered [MATH: x,y,z] on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

[MATH: x + y − 3z = 5; − 7x − y + z = 0; 2x + y − 2z = − 2]

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

[MATH: \left\lbrack
\matrix {
1 & 1 & -3 \
-7 & -1 & 1 \
2 & 1 & -2
}
\right\rbrack]

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

[MATH: 1|1|− 3|5; − 7|− 1|1|0; 2|1|− 2|− 2]

Item 12 — Example: Finding the Augmented Matrix of a Linear System With Variables Other Than x, y, z

Example Prompt:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

[MATH: {(c)/(2) = a; 5 + 3b − a = 4c; d = 1]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered [MATH: a,b,c,d] on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:
